overall: As of 8:20 AM ET, Atlanta sits at 69.8°F with a running max of 73.4°F, and morning warming has completely stalled — velocity is 0.0°F/hr and the running max has been flat since at least 7:00 AM. The elevated dewpoint of 62.6°F combined with calm winds suggests moisture or cloud cover is suppressing early morning solar heating, a pattern that could limit afternoon peak temperatures.
forecast_obs_notes: The primary model trio shows moderate disagreement: ECMWF (77.0°F) and HRRR (76.8°F) are tightly clustered and mutually reinforcing, while NBM runs about 2°F hotter at 79.2°F. More notably, the ensemble models are bimodally split — the even model flags 74-75°F and the odd model flags 81-82°F, both at the same 29% confidence tier — signaling genuine regime uncertainty about how aggressively afternoon heating will develop.
max_temp_prediction: The stalled morning warm-up and suppressed velocity at this hour favor the lower end of the forecast envelope, giving the ECMWF/HRRR consensus near 77°F the most credibility. The high dewpoint and calm winds may limit the boundary layer mixing needed to drive temperatures toward the NBM or odd-ensemble targets of 79-82°F, though some acceleration is still expected as the day progresses into peak heating hours. Confidence is moderate — the bimodal ensemble split is a caution flag — but the balance of evidence points to a daily high in the upper 70s.
